correctness.rationale: For every binary cross-type edge, the conformist and rebel utilities sum exactly to its weight. The sum of unilateral regrets is therefore half the two kernel residual 1-norms, and it vanishes precisely when all players best respond (including pure and partially mixed profiles). The origin is relative-interior to the box intersection, establishing dimension by rank-nullity. Nonzero determinant matching monomial and independent atomless weights prove generic rank, and a single nontrivial edge-weighted sign balance condition precludes pure equilibria almost surely. Exact standalone fractions-based verification checked 1,953 mixed profiles and all 256 positive integer 2-by-2 matrices with entries 1..4. Finite checks corroborate rather than replace the proof.

value.rationale: Recent conformist/rebel network literature predominantly asks for pure Nash equilibria or dynamics; in strongly heterophilous networks pure equilibria can fail while mixed Nash always exist. Classifying the entire Nash set, including boundary profiles, is a natural complete question. The exact matching-deficiency dimension gives a graph-theoretic measurement of mixed-equilibrium freedom and a perfect-matching criterion for generic uniqueness; the simultaneous almost-sure extinction of pure equilibria sharply contrasts with highly symmetric unweighted networks. This is structural mathematical content, not an arbitrary numerical recomputation. Value is limited to two actions, cross-group-only reciprocal weights and independent mixing.
